title: Airway Physiology: Ventilation vs Oxygenation for the PCP
next: Chapter 13, Lesson 2: Assessing breathing with pulse oximetry and capnography

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already open airways, suction, insert OPAs and NPAs, and ventilate with a BVM. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Review the airway landmarks that change your decisions
  2. Tell a ventilation problem from an oxygenation problem
  3. See why the PCP's CPAP and PEEP work, and when they don't

Textbook: Chapter 13, PDF pages 911–938
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter thirteen: airway management and ventilation. As EMRs, your basic airway skills are already solid. You open the airway, suction, insert oral and nasal airways, give oxygen, and ventilate with a bag-valve mask, or BVM. Now that you're practising as a PCP, you need to understand what's happening inside the chest, because your new tools depend on it. Today we cover three things. First, the airway landmarks that actually change your decisions. Second, the difference between a ventilation problem and an oxygenation problem. And third, why the two PCP tools, CPAP, or continuous positive airway pressure, and PEEP, or positive end-expiratory pressure, work, and when they don't.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第十三章：气道管理与通气。作为 EMR，你们的基础气道技能已经很扎实：开放气道、吸引、放口咽和鼻咽通气道、给氧，用球囊面罩（BVM）通气。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你需要明白胸腔里到底发生了什么，因为你的新工具要靠这些原理。今天讲三件事：第一，真正会改变你决策的气道解剖标志；第二，通气问题和氧合问题的区别；第三，PCP 的两样工具——CPAP（持续气道正压）和 PEEP（呼气末正压）——为什么有效，什么时候无效。

slides.title: Why airway failure kills
slides.body:
Brain damage after about 6 minutes without oxygen

  • Two jobs: bring in O₂, remove CO₂
  • Preventable deaths: basics not used or done badly
  • Wrong mask size, poor seal, poor head position
  • Rushing to advanced airways; not reassessing

Basic first, then advanced, and reassess after every step.
slides.say: Let's start with why this chapter matters. The respiratory system has two simple jobs: bring oxygen in and take carbon dioxide out. Carbon dioxide is the main waste product of the body's energy production. If oxygen stops, the brain lasts only about six minutes before permanent damage begins. Many preventable airway deaths are not caused by missing fancy equipment. They come from basic skills that weren't used, or were done badly: the wrong mask size, a leaking seal, poor head position. Others come from rushing to an advanced airway, or from not reassessing. Having more tools as a PCP never replaces good basics.
slides.sayZh: 先说这一章为什么重要。呼吸系统的工作很简单：把氧气带进来，把二氧化碳排出去；二氧化碳是身体产生能量时的主要废物。一旦断氧，大脑只能撑大约六分钟，之后就开始出现永久损伤。很多本可避免的气道死亡，并不是因为缺少高级设备，而是基础技术没用上或做得不好——面罩尺寸不对、密封漏气、头位不对。还有的是急着上高级气道，或者没有复评。作为 PCP 工具更多了，但永远替代不了扎实的基本功。

slides.title: Upper airway: landmarks that matter
slides.body:
Tonguemost common obstructionfalls back when LOC drops
Glottisnarrowest point in adultslaryngospasm can close it
Cricoidonly complete ringmembrane above it: surgical airway site
  • Nose: very rich blood supply; a rough NPA can bleed badly
  • Clear fluid from nose or ears after trauma: think skull fracture
slides.say: Here are the upper airway landmarks that change what you do. First, the tongue. When the level of consciousness drops, the jaw relaxes and the tongue falls back. It's the most common anatomical cause of obstruction. Second, the glottis, the opening between the vocal cords. It's the narrowest part of the adult airway, and a spasm of the cords, called laryngospasm, can close it. Third, the cricoid cartilage, the only complete ring in the upper airway. The membrane just above it is where surgical airways are done, which isn't on the BC PCP licensing exam. The nose has a rich blood supply, so a rough nasal airway can cause bleeding that pressure won't stop. And clear fluid from the nose or ears after head trauma suggests a skull fracture.
slides.sayZh: 这些上气道标志会改变你的处理。第一是舌头：意识下降时下颌松弛、舌后坠，这是解剖性气道梗阻最常见的原因。第二是声门，也就是两侧声带之间的开口，是成人气道最窄处；声带痉挛，叫喉痉挛，可以把它关闭。第三是环状软骨，上气道唯一完整的软骨环；它上方的膜是做外科气道的位置，BC 的 PCP 执照考试不考这项操作。鼻腔血供丰富，鼻咽通气道放得粗暴，可能引起压迫都止不住的出血。头部外伤后鼻子或耳朵流出清亮液体，提示颅骨骨折。

slides.title: Lower airway, and why kids differ
slides.body:
• Trachea splits at the carina; right bronchus is shorter, straighter
  • Gas exchange happens in the alveoli
In a childSo you…
Large occiput: neck flexes when flatTowel under the shoulders
Big tongue, small jawExpect tongue obstruction
Under 10: narrowest at the cricoidKnow it for the exam
Soft chest, belly breathingWatch the abdomen
slides.say: Below the glottis is the lower airway. The trachea divides at the carina into two main bronchi. The right one is shorter and straighter, so things that go too deep often end up on the right. Air then reaches the alveoli, the tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens. Children are different. A child has a large back of the head, called the occiput, so lying flat bends the neck forward and can block the airway. A folded towel under the shoulders keeps the head neutral. The tongue is large and the jaw small. Under about age ten, the narrowest point is the cricoid ring, not the glottis. And children breathe mostly with the diaphragm, so watch the belly, not just the chest.
slides.sayZh: 声门以下是下气道。气管在隆突处分成左右主支气管，右侧更短更直，所以下得太深的东西常常进到右边。空气再到达肺泡，也就是进行气体交换的小气囊。儿童不一样。孩子后脑勺（枕部）大，平躺时脖子被顶得前屈，可能堵住气道；在肩下垫一条折好的毛巾，让头保持中立位。孩子舌头大、下颌小。大约十岁以下，最窄处在环状软骨环，而不是声门。孩子主要靠膈肌呼吸，所以要看肚子，而不只是看胸口。

slides.title: Volumes: fast and shallow fails
slides.body:
Alveolar air/min = (VT − VD) × RR

  • Tidal volume (VT): about 500 mL (5–7 mL/kg)
  • Dead space (VD): about 150 mL, no gas exchange
  • Normal: (500 − 150) × 16 = 5,600 mL/min, good
  • Fast, shallow: (200 − 150) × 40 = 2,000 mL/min, failing
slides.say: Now the most useful formula in this chapter. Tidal volume is the size of one breath, about five hundred millilitres in an adult, or five to seven millilitres per kilogram. But about one hundred fifty millilitres of every breath stays in the dead space, the trachea and large bronchi, where no gas exchange happens. So what really matters is minute alveolar volume: tidal volume minus dead space, times the rate. A normal adult gets about five thousand six hundred millilitres per minute to the alveoli. Now take a patient breathing forty times a minute, but only two hundred millilitres each time. Only fifty per breath reaches the alveoli: two thousand per minute. The rate looks busy, but the patient is failing. As a PCP, judge depth, not just rate.
slides.sayZh: 接下来是本章最有用的公式。潮气量是一次呼吸的量，成人约五百毫升，也就是每公斤五到七毫升。但每口气里大约一百五十毫升停留在死腔，也就是气管和大支气管，那里不进行气体交换。所以真正重要的是分钟肺泡通气量：潮气量减去死腔，再乘以呼吸频率。正常成人每分钟约有五千六百毫升到达肺泡。现在看一个病人，每分钟呼吸四十次，但每次只有二百毫升：每口只有五十毫升到达肺泡，每分钟两千毫升。频率看着很忙，病人其实在衰竭。作为 PCP，要看深度，不只看频率。

slides.q: You find a man breathing 36 times a minute with very shallow breaths and minimal chest rise. What is the main concern?
options: His minute volume is too high, so he is blowing off too much oxygen
Much of each breath stays in dead space, so too little air reaches the alveoli
He is hyperventilating from anxiety and only needs coaching
His fast rate guarantees adequate gas exchange
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. You find a man breathing thirty-six times a minute with very shallow breaths and minimal chest rise. What is the main concern? A, his minute volume is too high, so he is blowing off too much oxygen. B, much of each breath stays in dead space, so too little air reaches the alveoli. C, he is hyperventilating from anxiety and only needs coaching. D, his fast rate guarantees adequate gas exchange. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你发现一名男子每分钟呼吸三十六次，非常浅，胸廓几乎不起伏。主要担心的是什么？A，他的分钟通气量太高，把氧气呼掉太多了；B，每口气大部分停在死腔，到达肺泡的空气太少；C，他是焦虑性过度通气，只需要安抚引导；D，呼吸快就保证了气体交换充分。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. With very small breaths, much of each one only fills the dead space of about one hundred fifty millilitres, so alveolar ventilation drops even though the rate is high. A is wrong because the problem isn't blowing off oxygen; it's too little fresh air reaching the alveoli. C is unlikely: an anxious patient usually breathes deep and fast, not shallow with poor chest rise. D is the trap: a fast rate never guarantees good ventilation.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。呼吸很小时，每口气大部分只填满约一百五十毫升的死腔，所以即使频率很快，肺泡通气量也会下降。A 错，因为问题不是把氧呼掉，而是到达肺泡的新鲜空气太少。C 不太可能：焦虑的病人通常是又深又快，而不是浅、胸廓起伏差。D 正是陷阱：呼吸快从来不能保证通气良好。

slides.title: Breathing in: negative pressure
slides.body:
Diaphragm and intercostals contract→chest gets bigger→pressure falls, air flows in
  • Breathing in is active; breathing out is passive
  • Too little effort: no negative pressure, no air
  • The only fix: positive pressure (pocket mask, BVM)
  • Positive pressure raises chest pressure: less blood back to the heart
slides.say: How does air get in? The diaphragm contracts and flattens, and the intercostal muscles lift the ribs up and out. The chest gets bigger, the pressure inside falls below the air outside, and air flows in. This is negative pressure ventilation. Breathing out is passive: the lungs simply spring back. When a patient is apneic, or the breaths are too small, there's no negative pressure, and no amount of oxygen flow will help. The only fix is to push air in: positive pressure, with a pocket mask or a BVM. Also, positive pressure raises the pressure inside the chest and slows blood returning to the heart. That's why over-ventilating is harmful, and why CPAP and PEEP can lower the blood pressure.
slides.sayZh: 空气是怎么进来的？膈肌收缩变平，肋间肌把肋骨向上向外抬起，胸腔变大，里面的压力低于外面，空气就流进来，这叫负压通气。呼气是被动的：肺自己弹性回缩。病人呼吸停止，或者每口气太小，就没有负压，这时氧流量开多大都没用，唯一的办法是把空气压进去，也就是正压通气，用口袋面罩或 BVM。另外，正压会升高胸腔内压力，减慢血液回流心脏。所以过度通气有害，CPAP 和 PEEP 也可能让血压下降。

slides.title: What drives breathing
slides.body:
• Main drive: CO₂, sensed through the pH of the spinal fluid
  • More CO₂ → more acid → faster, deeper breathing
  • Backup: hypoxic drive (low O₂), usually only end-stage COPD
  • Faster: fever, pain, hypoxia, acidosis. Slower: opioids, sleep
  • BC: COPD and short of breath → high-flow O₂ is indicated
  • Then nasal cannula at 1–3 L/min
slides.say: What tells us to breathe? The brainstem controls breathing, and the main signal is carbon dioxide. When carbon dioxide rises, the fluid around the brain becomes more acidic, and sensors there tell us to breathe faster and deeper. Low oxygen is only a backup signal, called the hypoxic drive, usually seen only in end-stage COPD, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Fever, pain, hypoxia and acidosis speed breathing up; opioids and sleep slow it down. Here's the BC point. Don't hold back oxygen from a COPD patient who is short of breath because you fear the hypoxic drive. The BC guideline says high-flow oxygen is indicated, and then a nasal cannula at one to three litres per minute.
slides.sayZh: 是什么让我们呼吸？脑干控制呼吸，主要信号是二氧化碳。二氧化碳升高时，脑周围的液体变酸，那里的感受器就让我们呼吸更快更深。低氧只是备用信号，叫低氧驱动，一般只见于终末期 COPD，也就是慢性阻塞性肺病。发热、疼痛、缺氧、酸中毒会让呼吸加快；阿片类药物和睡眠会让它变慢。这里有个 BC 要点：不要因为担心低氧驱动，就不给呼吸急促的 COPD 病人氧气。BC 指南写明这时应给高流量氧，之后再改为鼻导管每分钟一到三升。

slides.title: Ventilation vs respiration
slides.body:
Ventilationmoving air in and outfails: CO₂ builds up
External respirationalveoli ↔ bloodfails: O₂ can't get in
Internal respirationblood ↔ cellsneeds hemoglobin and flow

Good air movement does not guarantee good gas exchange.
slides.say: Two words sound similar but mean different things. Ventilation is the mechanical act of moving air in and out of the lungs. Respiration is gas exchange, by diffusion. External respiration is between the alveoli and the blood; internal respiration is between the blood and the cells. About ninety-seven percent of the oxygen in blood rides on hemoglobin, and most carbon dioxide travels as bicarbonate. It matters because a patient can move plenty of air and still have poor gas exchange. Think of a patient with lungs full of fluid. Air goes in and out, but oxygen can't cross the wet alveoli. As a PCP, you'll match your treatment to the step that is broken.
slides.sayZh: 有两个词听起来很像，意思却不同。通气是把空气搬进搬出肺的机械动作。呼吸指气体交换，靠扩散完成。外呼吸发生在肺泡和血液之间，内呼吸发生在血液和细胞之间。血液里大约百分之九十七的氧靠血红蛋白携带，大部分二氧化碳以碳酸氢根的形式运输。这很重要，因为病人可能空气进出很多，气体交换却很差。想想肺里充满液体的病人：空气进进出出，但氧气穿不过湿透的肺泡。作为 PCP，你要针对坏掉的那一步来处理。

slides.title: Two kinds of failure
slides.body:
O₂ can't get in (oxygenation)Air isn't moving (ventilation)
Wet alveoli: pulmonary edema, pneumoniaSlow, shallow: opioids, head injury
Less surface: pneumothorax, flail chestWeak muscles: spinal cord injury
Can't carry O₂: bleeding, CO poisoningResult: CO₂ builds up

Left: oxygen, and the PCP may add CPAP. Right: ventilate with a BVM.
slides.say: So on scene, ask yourself: is this patient failing to get oxygen in, or failing to move air? Oxygenation problems come from wet alveoli, like pulmonary edema or pneumonia; from less lung surface, like a pneumothorax or flail chest; or from blood that can't carry oxygen, like heavy bleeding or carbon monoxide, which binds hemoglobin about two hundred fifty times more strongly than oxygen. Ventilation problems mean carbon dioxide builds up: slow, shallow breathing from opioids or a head injury, or weak breathing muscles. Many patients have both. The treatment follows the problem. Poor oxygenation in a patient who still breathes well enough needs oxygen, and as a PCP you may add CPAP. Poor ventilation needs a BVM. More oxygen alone won't fix it.
slides.sayZh: 所以在现场要问自己：这个病人是氧气进不去，还是空气搬不动？氧合问题来自湿透的肺泡，比如肺水肿、肺炎；来自肺的交换面积变小，比如气胸、连枷胸；或者血液运不了氧，比如大出血或一氧化碳中毒——一氧化碳和血红蛋白的结合力大约是氧的二百五十倍。通气问题意味着二氧化碳在体内堆积：阿片类或颅脑外伤造成的呼吸慢而浅，或者呼吸肌无力。很多病人两种问题都有。处理要跟着问题走：自主呼吸还够、但氧合差的病人需要给氧，作为 PCP 你还可以加 CPAP；通气不足的病人需要 BVM，光加氧解决不了。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: CHF / pulmonary edema
slides.body:
BC protocol: congestive heart failure or pulmonary edema (also drowning, cardiogenic shock, toxic exposure)

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Rest; sit upright, legs down; keep warm
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if altered LOC or SpO₂ < 94%
  • Transport

PCP adds (on scene)

  • Consider CPAP
  • If BVM ventilation is needed: consider a PEEP valve, 5 cmH₂O to start
slides.say: Let's link this to the BC protocol for congestive heart failure or pulmonary edema. It's the classic oxygenation problem: fluid in the alveoli. The left column is what you already do: rest, sit the patient up with the legs down, keep them warm, give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher, and assist ventilations if consciousness drops or the saturation stays under ninety-four. The right column is new. On scene, the PCP considers CPAP. And if BVM ventilation is needed, the PCP can add a PEEP valve, starting at five centimetres of water. Both keep the alveoli open so oxygen can cross. We'll practise them in Lesson three.
slides.sayZh: 把这些和 BC 的充血性心衰或肺水肿流程联系起来。这是典型的氧合问题：肺泡里有液体。左栏是你本来就做的：休息，让病人坐直、双腿下垂，保暖，给氧使血氧维持在百分之九十四以上；如果意识下降或血氧一直低于九十四，就辅助通气。右栏是新的：PCP 在现场考虑使用 CPAP；如果需要 BVM 通气，PCP 可以加一个 PEEP 阀，起始五厘米水柱。两者都让肺泡保持张开，氧气就能过去。第三课会详细练。

slides.q: A heroin overdose patient responds only to pain. He breathes 6 times a minute, shallow, with SpO₂ 86%. As a PCP, what is your first priority?
options: Non-rebreather mask at 15 L/min, and watch the SpO₂
Ventilate with a BVM and oxygen
Start an IV before doing anything else
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. A patient who overdosed on heroin responds only to pain. He's breathing six times a minute, shallow, with a saturation of eighty-six percent. As a PCP, what is your first priority? A, a non-rebreather mask at fifteen litres per minute, and watch the saturation. B, ventilate with a BVM and oxygen. C, apply CPAP at five centimetres of water. D, start an IV before doing anything else. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名海洛因过量的病人只对疼痛有反应，每分钟呼吸六次、很浅，血氧百分之八十六。作为 PCP，你的第一优先是什么？A，非重复呼吸面罩每分钟十五升，然后观察血氧；B，用 BVM 加氧气通气；C，上 CPAP，五厘米水柱；D，先开静脉再做别的。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. This is a ventilation problem: the patient isn't moving enough air, so the first fix is to breathe for him with a BVM and oxygen. Secure ventilation first; naloxone comes after. A is wrong because a non-rebreather depends on the patient's own breaths, and his are too small. C is wrong because BC lists decreased level of consciousness, hypoventilation and respiratory arrest as contraindications to CPAP. D delays the airway; an IV is never the first priority here.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。这是通气问题：病人搬动的空气不够，所以第一步是用 BVM 加氧气替他呼吸。先保证通气，纳洛酮在后。A 错，因为非重复呼吸面罩靠病人自己吸气，而他的呼吸太小。C 错，BC 把意识下降、通气不足和呼吸停止列为 CPAP 的禁忌证。D 耽误了气道处理，这时静脉通路永远不是第一优先。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A fast rate can hide poor alveolar ventilation
  • Good SpO₂ on oxygen does not prove good ventilation
  • Don't withhold O₂ from COPD out of fear of hypoxic drive
  • Positive pressure (BVM, CPAP, PEEP) can drop the BP
  • CO poisoning: hemoglobin is blocked, not the airway
slides.say: Now the things you never had to think about this deeply as an EMR. First, a fast rate can hide poor alveolar ventilation, so always look at chest rise. Second, a good saturation on high-flow oxygen does not prove the patient is ventilating well. Saturation tells you about oxygen, not carbon dioxide, and carbon dioxide can keep building while the number looks fine. Third, don't withhold oxygen from a COPD patient in distress. Fourth, every form of positive pressure, a BVM, CPAP or PEEP, raises the pressure in the chest and can lower the blood pressure, so you'll check it more often. And fifth, in carbon monoxide poisoning, hemoglobin is blocked, so the problem is carrying oxygen, not moving air.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲你当 EMR 时不必想得这么深、现在要注意的事。第一，快速的呼吸可能掩盖肺泡通气不足，所以一定要看胸廓起伏。第二，在高流量氧下血氧很好，并不能证明病人通气良好。血氧反映的是氧，不是二氧化碳；数字好看的同时，二氧化碳可能在继续堆积。第三，不要不给处于窘迫中的 COPD 病人吸氧。第四，各种正压——BVM、CPAP、PEEP——都会升高胸腔压力、可能降低血压，所以你要更频繁地测血压。第五，一氧化碳中毒时血红蛋白被占住了，问题在于运氧，而不在于搬动空气。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Judge breathing by depth and rate: fast and shallow can be failing
  2. Ventilation (air) is not respiration (gas exchange): match the fix
  3. PCP adds CPAP and PEEP for oxygenation; hypoventilation needs a BVM

Next: assessing breathing with pulse oximetry and capnography
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: judge breathing by depth and rate together. Fast and shallow can mean the patient is failing, because dead space eats each small breath. Two: ventilation is moving air, and respiration is gas exchange. A patient can do one well and the other badly, so match your fix to the failure. Three: as a PCP you add CPAP and the PEEP valve, which help oxygen cross wet or collapsed alveoli. But a patient who isn't breathing enough needs you to ventilate with a BVM; CPAP won't do it. Next lesson, we'll assess breathing in more depth, with pulse oximetry and capnography. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，判断呼吸要把深度和频率放在一起看：又快又浅可能说明病人正在衰竭，因为死腔把每一小口气都吃掉了。二，通气是搬动空气，呼吸是气体交换；病人可能一样做得好、另一样做得差，所以处理要对准坏掉的那一步。三，作为 PCP，你多了 CPAP 和 PEEP 阀，它们帮助氧气穿过湿透或塌陷的肺泡；但呼吸不够的病人需要你用 BVM 通气，CPAP 做不到。下节课我们更深入地讲怎么评估呼吸，包括脉搏血氧和二氧化碳描记。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
